title: An In Vitro Enzymatic Assay to Measure Transcription Inhibition by Gallium(III) and H3 5,10,15-tris(pentafluorophenyl)corroles
protocol: Maintain a clean working environment to avoid contamination by DNase and RNase enzymes.
Wipe down lab surfaces and equipment with a decontamination solution.
Dissolve Actinomycin D in 1.8 ml of DMSO.
Aliquot 10 μl of the dissolved Actinomycin D into a separate container.
Dilute the aliquoted Actinomycin D to 1 ml with nuclease-free water.
Aliquot 1 μl of the diluted solution into another separate container.
Dilute the second aliquot to 1 ml with nuclease-free water.
Dissolve 1 mg triptolide in 0.64 ml DMSO.
Aliquot 1 µl of the solution and dilute to 1 ml with nuclease-free water to create a 1/1,000 dilution.
Aliquot 1 µl of the first dilution and dilute to 1 ml with nuclease-free water to create a second 1/1,000 dilution.
Dissolve 1 mg tpfc in 2.9 ml DMSO.
Aliquot 10 µl of the solution and dilute to 1 ml with nuclease-free water to create a 1/100 dilution.
Aliquot 1 µl of the first dilution and dilute to 1 ml with nuclease-free water to create a second 1/1,000 dilution.
Dissolve 1 mg Ga(tpfc) in 2.6 ml DMSO.
Aliquot 10 µl of the solution and dilute to 1 ml with nuclease-free water to create a 1/100 dilution.
Aliquot 1 µl of the first dilution and dilute to 1 ml with nuclease-free water to create a second 1/1,000 dilution.
Thaw on ice all frozen reagents.
Allow the 10x Reaction Buffer and ribonucleotide solutions time to mix until completely dissolved.
Briefly centrifuge all reagents to prevent loss of material on the rim of the tube.
Store ribonucleotides on ice while keeping the 10x Reaction Buffer at room temperature.
Combine reagents for transcription reaction at room temperature (refer to Table 2).
Mix thoroughly by flicking the tube or pipetting the mixture up and down gently.
Centrifuge briefly to collect reaction mixture at the bottom of the tube.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 37 °C for a total of 2-4 hours.
Remove 4 μl aliquots from each reaction after each hour.
Store aliquots at -20 °C.
Purify RNA using microcentrifuge-compatible chromatography columns following the transcription reaction.
Evenly resuspend the Sephadex matrix in the column buffer by flicking the column sharply three or more times.
Remove the top cap from the column and snap off the bottom tip of the column.
Place the column in a sterile 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 1,000 x g for 1 min to pack the matrix.
Discard the eluted buffer from the column.
Immediately place the column in a new sterile 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Pipette the sample to the center of the column bed using 20-50 μl of sample.
Centrifuge the tube at 1,000 x g for 1 min to elute the RNA sample.
Dissolve 5 mg ethidium bromide in 10 ml water to make a 1,000x stock solution (0.5 mg/ml).
Combine 2.0 M Tris-acetate with 0.05 M EDTA to prepare a 50x TAE buffer.
Adjust pH of the TAE buffer to 8.5.
Dissolve 10 g UltraPure Agarose in 1 L 1x TAE buffer to make a 1% agarose gel solution.
Melt the agarose with a conventional microwave oven.
Cool the agarose solution to 50 °C.
Add 1 ml of 1,000x ethidium bromide stock solution to the 1% agarose gel solution.
Gently swirl or invert in a closed container to mix the agarose and ethidium bromide solution thoroughly.
Pour the agarose-ethidium bromide mixture into a gel-casting platform.
Allow the gel to solidify at room temperature.
Place the set gel in the electrophoresis tank.
Add enough TAE buffer to cover the gel until the wells are submerged.
Check that the level of the TAE buffer is approximately 1 mm above the level of the gel.
Remove the gel comb.
Prepare RNA samples by combining 1 µl of each purified sample aliquot with 1 µl Gel Loading Buffer or with 1 µl 10x loading buffer and diluted to 10 µl with nuclease-free water.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down with a micropipette.
Load the gel with each sample by carefully pipetting the solution into the bottom of each well.
Take care not to leave any air bubbles or mix samples between wells.
Attach the leads so that the DNA will migrate into the gel towards the positive lead.
Set the voltage to the desired level, typically 1 to 10 V/cm of gel.
Run the gel for however long is sufficient for significant separation between the RNA fragments.
Place 2 μl H2O on a NanoDrop 2000 and measure the Blank.
Measure UV-Vis from a wavelength range of 200 nm to 800 nm for each RNA sample following purification.
Dilute samples in nuclease-free water if absorbance is above 1 O.D.
